title: Rosalind and the Autopsy
premise: When the coffin of Harrow's Crossing founder Elias Wren is exhumed for a cemetery relocation, night-shift taxi dispatcher Gideon Yarrow discovers the body inside belongs to a stranger — and the real Wren vanished forty years ago, on the same night Gideon's father drove the founder's last fare. Using the taxi company's decades-old dispatch logs, Gideon traces the route Wren took that night and realizes the killer has been quietly erasing witnesses ever since, including people Gideon loves. To close the case before the statute expires, Gideon must stage a fake autopsy of the stranger in the coffin and let the killer come to destroy the evidence. The trap works: the killer is the town archivist, Wren's illegitimate son, who killed his father to inherit a name that was never given to him — and Gideon, having survived by belonging to no one, finally chooses the found family that chose him back.
about_author: B. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former small-town records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing other people's unfinished stories. They write mysteries about people who keep towns running after dark, and live somewhere with bad cell reception on purpose.

chapters.title: The Grave That Answered Wrong
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Gideon's POV. During a cemetery relocation, the coffin of founder Elias Wren is opened before town dignitaries — and the skull inside has a bullet hole Wren's death certificate never mentioned. Gideon, called to drive the coroner, watches the town's founding myth crack open. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. We learn Gideon's world: the dispatch office, the drivers who are his only family, his rule that every case gets closed. The police ask him to pull forty-year-old fare logs; he agrees too quickly, hungry for a puzzle bigger than his loneliness. Beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: A Stranger Wearing a Founder
chapters.summary: Coroner Priya Nair's POV. The autopsy reveals the body is not Wren: wrong age, old mining injuries, a stranger's dental work. Priya and Gideon quietly agree to keep one detail from the sheriff — the body's hands were bound before burial. Beat: complicity, the first secret shared.

chapters.title: The Last Fare
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the archive of dispatch ledgers, Gideon finds the final entry logged by his own father the night Wren disappeared: a run to the old quarry road, fare prepaid, passenger never registered as arriving. His father's handwriting stops mid-line. Beat: the case turns personal.

chapters.title: Everyone Loved Elias
chapters.summary: Multi-scene, Gideon's POV. Townsfolk recount Wren's generosity — the scholarships, the rebuilt church — but each account contains a small impossibility. Gideon realizes the town's love for Wren is a story maintained on purpose, and someone still tends it. Beat: unease beneath nostalgia.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon consults Maren Voss, the town archivist who has curated Wren's legacy for decades. Maren is helpful, brilliant, unsettlingly precise about the case file — she corrects Gideon's memory of a detail he never told her. Beat: the reader's first glimpse of the killer hiding in plain sight.

chapters.title: Quarry Road
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon walks his father's final route at night and finds a rusted lockbox in the quarry's flooded shelf: Wren's real will, naming an illegitimate son, plus a photograph of a boy. Someone has searched this spot before — recently. Beat: the past is not finished with anyone.

chapters.title: What the Drivers Saw
chapters.summary: Alternating driver POVs. Old-timer Cass recalls driving a frightened young woman to the bus station the week Wren vanished; a retired dispatcher admits logs were altered by 'someone from the foundation.' Gideon maps a pattern: every witness to that night has died or left. Beat: the conspiracy acquires a shape.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Deadline
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The statute of limitations on the oldest charges expires in five weeks, and the sheriff, facing re-election, wants the case closed as 'historical misidentification.' Gideon refuses to sign off, burning a bridge and his only official access. Beat: defiance at a cost.

chapters.title: House of the Founder
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Searching the Wren house museum after hours, Gideon finds the boy from the photograph in a hidden room — and a second, newer set of fingerprints in the dust. Maren's car is in the lot. She claims she was 'checking an inventory discrepancy.' Beat: cat and mouse, politely conducted.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fraying
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Gideon's POV. Gideon's drivers throw their annual potluck; for one evening the case recedes. Then Cass's taxi is run off the road — she survives, shaken, and Gideon understands he has made his people into targets. Beat: warmth interrupted by guilt.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Ground-penetrating radar on the quarry road finds a second body: the young woman from the bus station, killed the same night as Wren. Two victims, one night, one shooter. Priya notices the case file has been accessed with a foundation keycard. Beat: the killer is inside the investigation.

chapters.title: Son of Nobody
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Records trace the boy in the photograph to a state home — Elias Wren's unacknowledged son, who as an adult changed his name and returned to Harrow's Crossing under a new identity. The list of candidates narrows to three. Gideon realizes he may already know him. Beat: the trap of suspicion.

chapters.title: A Case File Better Than Mine
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Someone mails Gideon a photocopy of his own working notes, annotated in a neat hand — corrections, even praise. The killer is reading his investigation in real time and wants him to know it. Gideon, terrified and exhilarated, decides to feed the file lies. Beat: hunter becomes lure.

chapters.title: The Fake Autopsy
chapters.summary: Priya and Gideon's POV, alternating. They stage a sealed 're-examination' of the coffin body, announcing publicly that a hidden locket found on the remains will be opened on a specific date. It's a fabrication — the locket doesn't exist — but it's bait no true heir can ignore. Beat: the trap is set with a lie.

chapters.title: What Gideon's Father Knew
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with a flashback chapter-within. Gideon deciphers his father's truncated ledger entry: his father drove Wren to the quarry, witnessed the argument between Wren and a teenage son, and was paid off — then spent his life drinking himself quiet. Gideon forgives him mid-investigation. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Locket Night
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At the announced opening, the archive's alarm trips and Maren Voss is caught inside the evidence room — but she's only the decoy she was manipulated into being, and she's hurt. Gideon realizes the killer used his own trap to frame her and get the room cleared. Beat: the plan fails beautifully.

chapters.title: The Name He Chose
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Reviewing foundation keycard logs, Gideon identifies the third candidate: Deputy Coroner Aldous Finch, the unacknowledged son, who spent forty years curating his father's legend while erasing every witness to his own existence. Gideon sets a second, private trap — he tells only Finch where the real will is hidden. Beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: Quarry Road, Again
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, night. Finch comes for the lockbox and finds Gideon waiting, recorder running. Finch confesses with terrible calm — he killed his father for refusing to give him a name, then spent a lifetime guarding the story that made him somebody. When he raises the gun, Gideon's drivers arrive, having tracked him. Beat: climax; survival by belonging.

chapters.title: The Statute Expires
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Finch is arrested for the fresh crimes his cover-up required; the old murder technically slips past the statute, and the town must live with that. Gideon closes the file anyway — his way — and donates the real will to the town, unredacted. Beat: justice imperfect but honest.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Autopsy
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The title's meaning lands: the stranger in the coffin was Rosalind Wren — Elias's sister, the true founder the legend erased, killed the same night. Priya performs the honest autopsy the town never gave her. Beat: the dead get their names back.

chapters.title: Open for Fares
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, epilogue. The dispatch office reopens after the funeral for a founder nobody knew. Cass drives again; Maren, cleared, re-catalogues the town's true history; Gideon, offered a better job elsewhere, stays. He takes a fare at 3 a.m. and, for the first time, doesn't need the case to feel like he belongs. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
